Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings:  33-year-old woman with first episode of unilateral throbbing headache and photophobia, relieved by darkness, no focal neurology, fever, or meningism. Family history of migraine; using estrogen-containing OCP; recent work stress.

Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):  
• Migraine without aura – highly likely given classic features and family history.  
• Tension-type/stress-related headache – moderate likelihood; pain description less typical.  
• Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – low–moderate likelihood due to OCP use; no focal deficits but must remain vigilant.

Working diagnosis:  Probable migraine without aura (first presentation).

Management priorities:  
1. Symptomatic treatment – add NSAID (ibuprofen) with paracetamol if no contraindication.  
2. Advise optimal hydration, rest in dark room.  
3. Safety-net advice – seek urgent review if headache worsens, new symptoms (fever, rash, neurological signs), or if persists.  
4. Arrange in-person BP check soon; consider further evaluation if headaches recur or become cyclical.  
5. Encourage acquisition of home thermometer for self-monitoring.  

Management Plan

- Medications:  Trial ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) in combination with paracetamol; avoid aspirin.  
- Education:  Hydration, trigger avoidance, monitor symptoms, red-flag advice given.  
- Follow-up:  Contact clinic if headache persists/worsens; routine BP check to be arranged; consider review for recurrent headaches.  
- No immediate investigations ordered during telehealth call.

- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded (may revisit if stress persists).  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  BP check advised; other preventive items not arranged.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: unilateral throbbing, photophobia, relief in dark, family history, appropriate demographic.  
2. Tension-type headache – Moderate likelihood: stress trigger, constant baseline pain without vomiting; less typical features (throbbing, photophobia) reduce likelihood.  
3. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Low–Moderate likelihood: new headache in woman on combined OCP; lacks focal signs or progressive course.
